\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Config Count: Results}

\begin{definition}[Configuration core data]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b006
}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
For a natural number $k$, a state type $S$, a Boolean input string $x$, and a
configuration $C$ of a $k$-tape machine on $x$, its core data are the tuple consisting
of its optional state, input-head position, work-tape contents, and work-tape head
positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-step evolution determined by the core]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols and state set $S$, and
let $c,d$ be configurations on input $x$ with equal cores. Then the configurations
obtained from $c$ and $d$ after one step have equal cores.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evolution determined by the core]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_runFrom}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols and state set $S$, and
let $c,d$ be configurations on input $x$ with equal cores. For every natural number $t$,
the configurations reached from $c$ and $d$ after $t$ steps have equal cores.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Distinct computation cores before halting]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_injOn}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_injOn}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $c$ be a
configuration on input $x$, and let $T$ be a natural number. Suppose the computation
from $c$ is halted at time $T$ and is not halted at any time $t<T$. Then for any
$t_1<t_2<T$, the cores of the configurations at times $t_1$ and $t_2$ are distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Attainment of intermediate integer values]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.exists_eq_of_between}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.exists_eq_of_between}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $p:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a sequence of integers with $p(0)=0$ and
$|p(j+1)-p(j)|\le 1$ for every natural number $j$. For every natural number $t$ and
integer $y$ lying between $0$ and $p(t)$, inclusive, in either order, there is an index
$j\le t$ such that $p(j)=y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Position bounded by the number of visited cells]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_pos_lt_card_visited}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_pos_lt_card_visited}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols and state set $S$, let
$x$ be a Boolean input, let $t\in\bbn$, and let $i<k$ be a work-tape index. If
$z\in\bbz$ is a position occupied by the head of tape $i$ at some time from $0$ through
$t$, inclusive, then $|z|$ is strictly less than the number of distinct positions
occupied by that head during those times.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A nonblank cell has been visited by its tape head]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none}

\leanok

be a Boolean input word, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$, $i$ be a work-tape index, and

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of space use]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_mono}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead_mono}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be a
configuration for a Boolean input string, and let $t,t'\in\mathbb{N}$ with $t\le t'$.
The total number of distinct work-tape cells visited from $c$ through step $t$ is at
most the number visited through step $t'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Windowed configuration core code]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a Boolean input string,
and let $C$ be a configuration of a $k$-tape machine on $x$. For a natural number $B$,
its windowed core code consists of its optional state and input-head position, together
with the work-tape contents restricted to positions $-B$ through $B$ and the work-tape
head positions encoded in a range of size $2B+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Injectivity of bounded core coding]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode_injOn}
\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ be a natural number and let $c,d$ be configurations of the same $k$-tape machine
on the same bit-string input, with state type $S$. Suppose that for each work tape, each
head position in $c$ and $d$ has absolute value at most $B$, and every cell containing a
symbol on either configuration has position of absolute value at most $B$. If the
bounded core codes of $c$ and $d$ agree, then their cores agree.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Space bounded by the configuration count]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.of_spaceUsed_le}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.of_spaceUsed_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.configBound, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_injOn, Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_pos_lt_card_visited, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead_mono}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x,w$ be Boolean
words, and let $t,s$ be natural numbers. If $M$ computes $w$ from $x$ within $t$ steps
and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells during those $t$ steps, then it computes $w$ from
$x$ within $(|Q|+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$ steps, where $Q$ is the state set of $M$
and $k$ is its number of work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Configuration bound under logarithmic space]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.configBound_logSpace_le}
\label{Turing.FinTM.configBound_logSpace_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.configBound}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with $k$ work tapes and
state set $Q$, and let $c,n\in\mathbb{N}$. Define $L(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ and
$B_M(n,s)=(|Q|+1)(n+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$. Then
\[
B_M\bigl(n,cL(n)\bigr)\le (|Q|+1)\,2\,2^{5kc+3k}(n+1)^{5kc+1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Config Count: Further results}

\begin{lemma}[Position bound from unit steps]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.exists_eq_of_between}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $p(0)=0$ and $|p(j+1)-p(j)|\le 1$ for every
natural number $j$. For any natural number $t$, every $z$ among $p(0),p(1),\ldots,p(t)$
satisfies $|z|<N$, where $N$ is the number of distinct values in that list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Occupied cells lie among visited head positions]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(c_j)_{j\in\bbn}$ be a sequence of configurations of a $k$-work-tape Turing
machine. Suppose every cell of every work tape is blank in $c_0$, and for each $j$,
either $c_{j+1}=c_j$ or $c_{j+1}$ is obtained by applying a single action to $c_j$. If
cell $z\in\bbz$ contains a symbol on tape $i$ in $c_t$, then $z$ is one of the head
positions of tape $i$ at some time from $0$ through $t$, inclusive.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of visited cells]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead_mono}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols and
state set $S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration on $x$.
If $t\leq t'$, then for every work-tape index $i$, the set of cells visited by tape $i$
from $c$ through step $t$ is contained in the set visited through step $t'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Shifted integer code]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode}
\leanok
For a natural number $B$ and an integer $z$, encode $z$ as the element of
$\mathrm{Fin}(2B+1)$ with value $\min(\,(z+B).toNat,\,2B\,)$, where $(z+B).toNat$ is the
natural-number conversion of $z+B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Injectivity of the bounded position code]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode_injOn}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode_injOn}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $B\in\bbn$, and let $z,z'\in\bbz$ satisfy $|z|\le B$ and $|z'|\le B$. If their
position codes with bound $B$ are equal, then $z=z'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Configuration count bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.configBound}
\label{Turing.FinTM.configBound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$.
Define its configuration bound by $(|Q|+1)(n+2)\,3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$, where $Q$ is the
state set of $M$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Time bound from logarithmic space]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.of_spaceUsed_le, Turing.FinTM.configBound_logSpace_le}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $f$ map binary words to
binary words, and let $c\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary input $x$, $M$
halts with output $f(x)$ after some number of steps and uses at most $c(\lfloor\log_2
|x|\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells. Then $M$ computes $f$ within the time bound
$T(n)=((|Q|+1)\,2\,2^{5kc+3k})(n+1)^{5kc+1}$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes and
$Q$ is the state set of $M$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Log space is contained in polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_P}
\label{Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime}
\difficulty{3}
Every language decidable by a finite Turing machine using space bounded by a constant
multiple of $\log_2(n)+1$ is decidable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Log-space computation implies polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_of_computesInSpace}
\label{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_of_computesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f$ be a function on bit strings, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine, and let $c$ be
a natural number. If for every input $x$ there is a time $t$ such that $M$ halts on $x$
with output $f(x)$ after $t$ steps and uses at most $c(\log_2 |x|+1)$ work-tape cells
through step $t$, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound persists after halting]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $\Sigma$, let $x,w$ be words over
$\Sigma$, and let $t,s$ be natural numbers. If $M$ computes $w$ from $x$ within $t$
steps and has used at most $s$ work-tape cells through step $t$, then for every natural
number $t'$, the total number of work-tape cells visited through step $t'$ is at most
$s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Time and space bounds from space-bounded computation]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.of_spaceUsed_le, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt, Turing.FinTM.configBound, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $f$ map binary words to
binary words, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input $x$, $M$
halts with output $f(x)$ at some time while using at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells. Then
$M$ computes $f$ within time $B(|x|,s(|x|))$, where
$B(n,r)=(|Q|+1)(n+2)3^{k(2r+1)}(2r+1)^k$, $k$ is the number of work tapes, and $Q$ is
its state set. Moreover, for every binary input $x$ and every time $t$, the computation
from the initial configuration on $x$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space-efficient alphabet reduction]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_of_alphabetReduction}
\label{Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_of_alphabetReduction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTimeVia, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction_spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an injection,
let $D$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $L$ be a language of binary
strings, and let $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary string $x$,
the machine $D$ computes the letterwise image under $e$ of the one-symbol output
indicating whether $x\in L$, on input the letterwise image of $x$; and suppose that for
every $\Gamma$-string $y$ and every time $t$, its computation from input $y$ uses at
most $S(|y|)$ space. Then there are a natural number $c$ and a finite Turing machine $M$
over the Boolean alphabet that decides $L$ using at most $c(S(n)+1)$ space on inputs of
length $n$.
\end{theorem}
